local_facts.claim: Jacksonville and Duval County consolidated in 1968. A City financial report describes the City/County area as 840.1 square miles, with four separate municipalities remaining within Duval County.
local_facts.why_it_matters: Emergency-plumbing routing cannot treat “Jacksonville” as one compact service area. The exact address establishes the response route and helps distinguish central neighborhoods from far-out Duval locations before a technician is dispatched.
local_facts.title: Jacksonville’s service map is much larger than a typical city call area

local_facts.claim: At a January 22, 2024 City meeting, the Septic Tank Phase Out Program reported 35 septic tank failure areas and approximately 23,000 failing septic tanks in Duval County. The program had four active areas: Biltmore, Beverly Hills, Christobel, and Riverview.
local_facts.why_it_matters: A wastewater backup cannot be assumed to be a public sewer-line problem. The property may use septic infrastructure or JEA sewer, and that distinction changes how the technician traces the failure and what repair can address it.
local_facts.title: Some Jacksonville backups start with septic, not sewer

local_facts.claim: A U.S. Geological Survey report states that, throughout most of Duval County, the water table is within 5 feet of land surface and can fluctuate as much as 5 feet between wet and dry seasons. City residential inspection guidance requires underground plumbing to be inspected before a slab inspection when plumbing is included in the project.
local_facts.why_it_matters: Water showing at a slab edge or through flooring needs careful locating before concrete is opened. The visible wet area may be some distance from the failed buried line, so an emergency repair begins with isolation and tracing rather than a guess at where to break the slab.
local_facts.title: Shallow groundwater makes under-slab water evidence worth tracing carefully

anchors.label: Minimum plumbing permit fee
anchors.detail: The floor for a plumbing permit under the city's fee schedule, regardless of how the itemized formula adds up on a small repair.
anchors.source_name: City of Jacksonville fee schedule, Section 320.409

anchors.label: Permit line for each fixture or sewer connection
anchors.detail: Charged per roughed-in fixture or plugged outlet, per building sewer connection, and per $100 of estimated cost on repairs to waste, soil, vent or building drain pipe.
anchors.source_name: City of Jacksonville fee schedule, Section 320.409

anchors.label: JEA sewer tap, six-inch connection
anchors.detail: What the utility charges to set a six-inch sewer connection, with a $2,894 tap extension fee where an existing tap only needs bringing to the property line.
anchors.source_name: JEA water and sewer system tariff

anchors.label: JEA water tap and meter set, three-quarter inch service
anchors.detail: The tap fee for a one-inch tap serving a three-quarter inch line, plus the meter set fee, charged before any plumbing contractor touches the house side of the meter.
anchors.source_name: JEA water and sewer system tariff
